ev.q: Being prescribed Paxlovid was associated with a lower hospitalization rate among the overall study population (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 0.49)
Association between Paxlovid receipt and subsequent hospitalization was assessed using a Cox proportional hazards model
Among the 198,927 Paxlovid recipients, 930 (0.47%) were hospitalized
among those who had received ≥3 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (aHR = 0.50)
Paxlovid receipt was associated with lower hospitalization rates among persons aged 18–49 years (aHR = 0.59, 95% CI = 0.48–0.71)
A retrospective analysis was performed on patient records included in Cosmos

methods_quotes.q: Association between Paxlovid receipt and subsequent hospitalization was assessed using a Cox proportional hazards model
Persons receiving Paxlovid contributed unexposed time until the prescription date and exposed time after the prescription date
primary analyses were repeated either excluding telemedicine visits, or excluding patients hospitalized during the 2 days after diagnosis
The proportional hazards assumption was evaluated by plotting hazard functions for each variable in the model.
95% CIs that exclude 1 were considered to be statistically significant.
Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, race and ethnicity, social vulnerability index, number of underlying health conditions
